title: Europe privacy-first edge launch enablement
content:
Purpose:
This doc is an internal enablement and messaging brief for our upcoming Europe "privacy-first" edge offering. It combines positioning, a short competitive note, an announcement draft for comms, and a sales enablement cheat-sheet aimed at fintech and regulated SaaS buyers across EU markets.

TL;DR (for execs and huddles):
- Product: Redwood Edge (privacy-first): a managed edge inference option with per-region data residency, VPC isolation, and KMS-native key control targeted at customers with strict data locality and compliance needs.
- Primary use cases: financial models (KYC, fraud scoring), healthcare triage assistants, legal document summarization with residency constraints.
- Differentiator: unified runtime (same API/rollout/telemetry) across hosted + dedicated + private, plus first-class regionally pinned edge nodes and integrated key management for EU data residency.
- Launch target: staged beta in DE/FR/SE, GA in Europe region by end of Q2 2025.

Audience personas (quick):
- Fintech platform PMM: cares about auditability, encryption-in-flight/at-rest, latency <100ms for 512-token interactions.
- Platform engineer (mid-enterprise): needs predictable per-customer capacity and per-tenant routing.
- Security/compliance lead: needs SOC2/ISO messaging, KMS/HSM integration, and data residency guarantees.

Positioning pillars (short bullets we’ll reuse in collateral):
1) Privacy-first by design: explicit data residency controls + optional customer-managed keys.
2) Production-grade latency: edge nodes optimized for low-latency inference with our serving runtime.
3) Operational continuity: same tooling (console, rollouts, tracing) whether you use hosted, dedicated, or private.
4) Cost controls: recommendations and auto-configs for batching/quantization tuned per workload to avoid surprise bills.

Competitive snapshot (high level, quick notes for sales):
- Large cloud vendors: provide region-local endpoints but lack LLM-serving opinionation (batching, KV caching). Often higher operational friction to match throughput SLAs.
- Niche inference vendors: strong on performance but limited in offering unified control plane across hosted/dedicated/private. Key-management integrations often add manual work.
- Open-source self-host: low cost but high ops surface; unsuitable for teams needing compliance SLAs and fast time-to-value.

Key objections and rebuttals (sales playbook snippets):
- "We can just use the cloud region endpoint": Rebuttal -> Cloud endpoints may not offer per-customer routing, KV caching optimizations, or integrated rollout controls; Redwood bundles runtime optimizations + policies that reduce token costs and improve p99 latency.
- "We need HSM-managed keys": Rebuttal -> We support KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated; for hosted edge we offer customer-managed keys via partner KMS where available.
- "What about vendor lock-in?": Rebuttal -> Our API and rollout primitives are identical across deployment modes; customers can start hosted and migrate to Dedicated/Private with minimal code changes.

Announcement draft (short — for PR/marketing tweak):
Headline: Redwood launches privacy-first edge inference for Europe, enabling low-latency, region-pinned LLM serving with customer key control
Lead: Today we’re announcing Redwood Edge — a new privacy-first inference option that gives European teams the performance of edge inference with explicit data residency and key management controls. Built on Redwood’s unified serving runtime, Edge lets engineering teams ship LLM-powered features without trading off latency, compliance, or operational visibility.
Callouts (bullets we can use in social/one-pagers):
- Region-pinned inference nodes for EU data residency
- Optional customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and VPC isolation
- Same API and rollout tools as Redwood Hosted and Dedicated

Internal enablement: one-pager for sales/AE (talking points):
- Elevator pitch (15s): Redwood Edge gives you EU-resident LLM inference with enterprise-grade controls and the same developer experience your teams already use.
- 2-min pitch (for discovery): Ask about data residency needs, expected p99 latency, and key management. If they say high compliance, flag for Solutions Eng (SE) pre-sales.
- Demo checklist: show console region pinning, key config screen, rollout to edge node, per-route latency dashboard, and token-cost breakdown.
- Pricing hints: edge is priced as a premium on top of hosted per-token; offer trials and pilot credits for pilots <6 months.

Launch ops and dependencies (short):
- Product: finalize region-pin UI and KMS onboarding flow (PR: GO-1283).
- Infra: capacity reservation in EU-edge pools + autoscaling policy for burst on bank-hour spikes.
- Legal: finalize DPA addendum and data processing addendum language for EU customers.
- Marketing: draft customer-facing page + one-pager for fintech vertical.
- Sales/SE: create pilot pack and a technical runbook for SE-led installs.

Customer-facing FAQ (short):
Q: How do you guarantee data residency?
A: Requests routed to region-pinned nodes and logs/metadata are stored in-region; customers can opt for full private deployment for additional isolation.

Q: Can we use our KMS/HSM?
A: Yes — Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys; hosted edge supports partner KMS integrations where available.

Q: What if we need lower latency than edge nodes provide?
A: We support hybrid routing — ultra-low latency customers can use Dedicated infra or on-prem private deployments.

Launch checklist (milestones and owners):
- Beta kickoff (invite-only): 2025-02-24 — Owner: Product (Rohit)
- SE pilot templates completed: 2025-03-10 — Owner: Solutions Eng (Gunnar)
- Legal DPA sign-off: 2025-03-17 — Owner: Legal (Sofia)
- Marketing landing + PR draft: 2025-03-24 — Owner: GTM Marketing
- GA (public availability): target 2025-06-30 — Owner: Go-to-market lead

Risk register (brief):
- Capacity underprovisioning in early hours -> Mitigate with burst pool and pre-warm for pilot customers.
- KMS integration edge cases across EU cloud partners -> Maintain a supported list and fallbacks; document clearly for SE.
- Customer misconceptions about "edge" vs "on-prem" -> Include clear matrix in collateral that compares Hosted / Edge / Dedicated / Private.

Open questions for leadership (to resolve during pre-launch review):
- Pricing model decision: flat premium vs percent uplift on per-token — need final by 2025-03-03.
- Level of audit/reporting we provide in hosted-edge vs Dedicated (what logs/retention).

Appendix: useful links and artifacts (internal)
- Beta sign-up sheet (sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1EdgeBetaSignups
- SE runbook draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-runbooks/pull/5
- Internal demo script (slides): https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/Edge-Demo-Script

Notes to self (informal):
- Need a short 1-page comparison table we can paste into SDR outreach sequences.
- Coordinate with EU partnerships for KMS vendor support (check with infra on required IAM changes).
- Prep a list of 3 pilot customers we can invite that represent fintech, health, and legal.

Last edited by Amelia — quick next actions: finalize pricing option draft (input from finance), confirm capacity knobs with infra, and schedule a 1-hour cross-functional pre-launch review next week.
